description: The hand-verified expected result for the positive Semgrep SARIF fixture, which is an unmodified captured excerpt of harness/artifacts/raw/semgrep.sarif. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.

fixture.excerpt_note: An unmodified captured excerpt of that artifact, in the sense AAP 0.6.2 requires: whole records selected, the enclosing structure preserved, and no field value edited. The 9 results are the raw artifact's own result objects at indexes 0, 55, 254, 267, 309, 1002, 1080, 1092 and 1109 of its 1162, retained in raw document order and complete down to their fingerprints, properties and region snippets; the 9 driver rules are the raw rule objects those results resolve through by ruleId, at raw indexes 122, 216, 620, 684, 826, 849, 1258, 1396 and 1564 of its 2126, retained in raw document order with their defaultConfiguration, help, helpUri, name, shortDescription, fullDescription and properties intact -- nothing stripped. version, $schema, the runs[0] key set, tool.driver.name, tool.driver.semanticVersion and the whole invocations array -- including all 179 toolExecutionNotifications entries -- are the raw artifact's own, and no member the raw artifact lacks was introduced, so run.originalUriBaseIds is absent here exactly as it is there. Only the JSON text differs: the raw artifact is written as one compact line and this excerpt is indented for review, which is why 'byte for byte' is asserted per JSON record under a canonical serialization rather than over the file's bytes.
fixture.excerpt_verification: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/test_sarif_adapter.py, RawArtifactProvenanceTests -- the per-record, per-rule and per-envelope-member comparison against the raw artifact. The sha256 above is a mutation tripwire for this run, not the provenance evidence: a digest a fixture owns can only prove self-consistency.
fixture.selection_rationale: Selected for spread rather than for outcome: nine distinct rule identifiers over six rule-id families after the shared opt.blitzy-harness.rules.semgrep-rules prefix (ai, dockerfile, java, javascript, python, scala), all three SARIF level literals this producer emits (one error, six warning, two note), matches against six of the twelve authoritative globs, and three python/pyspark paths of which one is a test module -- python/pyspark/tests/test_appsubmit.py -- which is in scope because it carries no src/test segment. No finding is judged, ranked or compared with any other tool's by the selection or by anything below.
fixture.features_moved_out_of_this_fixture: The authored cases the pre-rebuild fixture carried -- an originalUriBaseIds base map, a ruleIndex-with-no-ruleId result, and a rule listing three CVE identifiers out of ascending order -- now live in oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-semgrep-features.sarif, which is declared derived in its own expected file. None of them is reachable from captured output in this provisioning, which is why they are exercised from a fixture that says so rather than from one claiming to be a capture.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.root_independence: Every uri in this fixture is already root-relative, and the recorded path base for semgrep is the scan root itself, so joining onto the base and relativizing back to the root returns the uri unchanged. These rows therefore hold for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file. RootIndependenceTests re-runs the fixture under a temporary root to prove it rather than restate it.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the semgrep entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.sarif_uri_base_id_observed: %SRCROOT%, on the first location of every one of the nine results
resolution_context.uri_base_id_walk_consequence: The producer sets uriBaseId '%SRCROOT%' on every result and emits no run.originalUriBaseIds at all, so the SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.4.4 procedure cannot complete -- the documented producer gap at https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep/issues/10591. That outcome is eligible for the metadata-backed fallback, so each path resolves against the runner-recorded base rather than being rejected; with path_base kind none it would be a counted unresolvable_path rejection instead, which is the second branch DegenerateBaseTwoBranchTests asserts.
resolution_context.severity_source: No result in this fixture states a level of its own, and no rule carries properties.severity or properties.problem.severity, so every severity_native is the level its own rule states under defaultConfiguration.level -- SARIF 2.1.0's own derivation for a result that omits the property -- and every severity_norm comes from the SARIF level table: error High, warning Medium, note Low, none Info. That is a property of the captured artifact: measured over its 1162 results, none carries a level.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A SARIF result names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of runs[].results[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty authored keys, one path_kind_* per path kind and one severity_basis_* per severity basis.
counters_note: The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool -- multi_location_records, multi_valued_cwe_records, multi_valued_cve_records and non_filesystem_paths -- are all 0 for this fixture, and each zero is an observed property of the captured records rather than an omission: every result carries exactly one location, no rule carries more than one distinct CWE identifier, no rule string carries a CVE identifier at all, and every path names a file inside the scanned tree. rule_id_from_rule_id is 9 and rule_id_from_rule_index is 0 because every captured result states its own ruleId and none carries a ruleIndex; the indexed route is exercised by derived-semgrep-features.sarif. severity_from_rule_default_configuration is 9 for the reason resolution_context.severity_source records.

corroboration.note: All nine records this fixture excerpts also appear in the committed dataset's 9433 rows, matched on tool, rule_id, path and start_line, and every one of the twelve fields agrees with the rows below. That is corroboration recorded after the fact, not the source of these values: each value here was derived from the fixture and the authored contracts, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply.

rows.message: This if statement will always have the same behavior and is therefore unnecessary.

RegExp() called with a `name` function argument, this might allow an attacker to cause a Regular Expression Denial-of-Service (ReDoS) within your application as RegExP blocks the main thread. For this reason, it is recommended to use hardcoded regexes instead. If your regex is run on user-controlled input, consider performing input validation or use a regex checking/sanitization library such as https://www.npmjs.com/package/recheck to verify that the regex does not appear vulnerable to ReDoS.
